Observability Workbench

A developer-facing platform for tracing incidents, exploring service health, and reducing time-to-diagnosis across distributed systems.

Overview

Observability Workbench was designed to make complex operational data usable for engineers who need fast answers during incidents.

The product combined trace search, service summaries, and alert context into a single workflow so teams could move from detection to diagnosis without jumping between tools.

What I Built

I owned the information architecture, data modeling, and frontend implementation for the core monitoring workflows.

That included building a typed API layer, reusable dashboard components, and a project structure that kept the interface maintainable as the number of views expanded.

  • Built shared card, table, and chart wrappers to keep the UI consistent
  • Structured service and trace data so pages could be composed from small, typed building blocks
  • Added incident-friendly interaction patterns with fast scanning and low visual noise

Outcome

The result was a technical product that felt clear instead of dense, which made it easier to communicate engineering judgment and system-level thinking.
